hypotheses.text: Multi-gene 17q24.2 microdeletions encompassing both PSMD12 and BPTF manifest an augmented neurodevelopmental phenotype featuring significantly higher rates of postnatal microcephaly and craniofacial dysmorphism severity compared to isolated intragenic PSMD12 truncating variants.
hypotheses.rationale: Deep testing showed disagreement on whether 17q24 microdeletions diverge phenotypically from isolated PSMD12 loss-of-function variants. Because contiguous deletions can encompass BPTF, which independently causes syndromic developmental delay and postnatal microcephaly, haploinsufficiency of both genes may produce an additive or compounded phenotype rather than an identical presentation.

evidence.text: BPTF loss-of-function variants on 17q24.2 cause developmental delay/intellectual disability (10/10), speech delay (10/10), postnatal microcephaly (7/9), and dysmorphic features (9/10), demonstrating that microdeletions spanning both PSMD12 and BPTF involve contiguous gene effects.

source.title: Haploinsufficiency of the chromatin remodeler BPTF causes syndromic developmental and speech delay, postnatal microcephaly, and dysmorphic features
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: The BPTF variants were found in unrelated individuals aged between 2.1 and 13 years, who manifest variable degrees of developmental delay/intellectual disability (10/10), speech delay (10/10), postnatal microcephaly (7/9), and dysmorphic features (9/10).

hypotheses.text: Isolated intragenic PSMD12 loss-of-function variants are sufficient to recapitulate the complete core phenotypic triad of Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (intellectual disability, craniofacial dysmorphism, and skeletal/digital anomalies) without requiring contiguous gene deletion on 17q24.2.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolving whether whole-gene deletions diverge from intragenic variants requires determining if the classical multi-system phenotype appears in its full form when only PSMD12 is disrupted. If familial truncating mutations show 100% penetrance for intellectual disability, craniofacial, and skeletal manifestations, microdeletions share the same primary driver mechanism.

evidence.text: Six patients from two unrelated families harboring inherited truncating PSMD12 variants presented with 100% penetrance of developmental delay, intellectual disability, craniofacial anomalies, and skeletal anomalies, confirming PSMD12 haploinsufficiency alone drives the complete core syndrome.

source.title: Does It Run in Your Family? Inherited Truncating PSMD12 Variants Broaden the Phenotypic Spectrum of Stankiewicz‐Isidor Syndrome
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A

hypotheses.text: Large 17q24 microdeletions (>2 Mb) exhibit higher rates of prenatal lethality, severe neonatal respiratory compromise/early death, and complex limb malformations (e.g. equinovarus feet, widespread skeletal dysplasia) than intragenic PSMD12 variants due to contiguous deletion of neighboring genes such as KPNA2, PRKAR1A, and KCNJ2.
hypotheses.rationale: Case reports of cytogenetically visible or multi-megabase 17q24 deletions demonstrate perinatal death and severe anatomical malformations that are not typically reported in patients with point mutations or small indels in PSMD12.

evidence.text: A newborn with an interstitial deletion del(17)(q23.2q24.3) exhibited severe growth retardation, maldeveloped oralpharyngeal structures, digital anomalies, and died on day 17 of life from recurrent apnea.

source.title: Unique de novo interstitial deletion of chromosome 17, del(17) ...
source.quote: We describe a newborn with a novel interstitial deletion of the long arm of chromosome 17 [del (17) (q23.2q24.3)] who died on day of life 17 during a recurrent apneic episode. Her phenotype included severe growth retardation, multiple facial anomalies, maldeveloped oralpharyngeal structures, and digital and widespread skeletal anomalies.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of reported 17q24.2 microdeletions encompassing PSMD12 also encompass BPTF, and do deletion patients with BPTF involvement exhibit significantly lower head circumference z-scores than those with intact BPTF?
new_directions.rationale: Directly testing head circumference metrics across mapped breakpoints will determine if microcephaly in STISS is a contiguous-gene effect mediated by BPTF or intrinsic to PSMD12 proteasome dysfunction.

new_directions.question_text: Are visceral and genitourinary malformations (CAKUT, congenital heart defects) more prevalent in 17q24 microdeletions compared to intragenic PSMD12 truncating variants?
new_directions.rationale: Establishing exact numerator/denominator prevalence of CAKUT and cardiac defects stratified by variant class will resolve whether multi-organ involvement stems solely from PSMD12 or reflects contiguous regulatory/coding disruption.
